shippedAt.derivation: The loop is verbatim; the function around it is not. `wrap()` gives it a signature that returns the list, matching `local-check-propagation.ts` so the two files' numbers are comparable. Nothing here is a check of omamori#558 R1 on the code that shipped.
shippedAt.equivalence: bench/rust/propagation-equivalence.rs — `implicit` and `explicit` return the same value on all eleven inputs; `skips-unreadable` differs on all eight that contain an error.

on_error_control.instructions: `code` is one function that walks an iterator whose items are each either a value or an error. Take the case where one item is an error. What does the function do with the items after it?

criteria.stops_there: It stops at that item; the ones after it are never taken from the iterator
criteria.keeps_going: It goes on taking the items after it
criteria.cannot_determine: The code does not say what happens to the items after an error

on_error_result.instructions: Still `code`, still the case where one item is an error. What does the function return to its caller?

criteria.an_error: A failure — whatever the caller does with it, it is not a successful list
criteria.a_success_with_what_it_had: A success carrying the items it managed to take, without the failure
criteria.cannot_determine: The code does not say what is returned when an item is an error

on_error_control.instructions: Read `code`. Assume exactly this and nothing else: The file has been opened successfully. `reader.lines()` returns `Err(io_error)` at one iteration. Every other operation the function reaches succeeds. The iterator is finite. Under that condition: what does the function do with the items the iterator would yield after that one?

criteria.stops_there: It stops at that item; the ones after it are never taken from the iterator
criteria.keeps_going: It goes on taking the items after it
criteria.cannot_determine: The code does not say what happens to the items after an error

on_error_result.instructions: Read `code`. Assume exactly this and nothing else: The file has been opened successfully. `reader.lines()` returns `Err(io_error)` at one iteration. Every other operation the function reaches succeeds. The iterator is finite. Under that condition: what does the function return to its caller?

criteria.an_error: A failure — whatever the caller does with it, it is not a successful list
criteria.a_success_with_what_it_had: A success carrying the items it managed to take, without the failure
criteria.cannot_determine: The code does not say what is returned when an item is an error

condition.setup: The file has been opened successfully.
condition.others: Every other operation the function reaches succeeds.

an_error.why: the failed enumeration does not leave the function as a success

a_success_with_what_it_had.why: the entries taken before the error are returned as though the listing were complete

a_success_with_nothing.why: an enumeration that failed is returned as an empty listing

cannot_determine.why: the code shown does not say what is returned
